SddReconcile.keywords: reconcile, fix, sync-from-code, drift, spec-probe, bug-vs-spec-defect, problem-class, blast-radius, back-sync, sdd-reconcile
SddReconcile.Mission:
Restore the spec ⟷ code ⟷ task triangle after it desynced, then prove the repaired path. A separate skill (`/sdd-reconcile`) activates one of two modes: - **fix** — a finding / bug / review drove it: the spec is presumed right until the probe proves a spec defect. - **from-code** — code ran ahead of the spec: code is evidence, not automatic authority to rewrite the design.
The probe (`AX_PROBLEM_PROBES_SPEC`) classifies ownership, problem class, blast radius, and whether a spec delta is semantic. Remediation then follows its real owner: task-owned code always becomes a new ticket Round; semantic design changes go through the artifact-kind authoring flow and integrated review/publication before implementation; only genuinely task-free non-semantic metadata with an exact verifier may use the bounded direct path.
Input — findings / a bug / a review, OR "I changed code, formalize it". Output — merged design when design changed, reopened/created tasks when code must move, tracker state owned by ordinary execute, and one non-duplicated evidence chain for the chosen path.
SddReconcile.ContextExpectation: Reconcile adds only one mechanical command beyond the authoring/execute flows it delegates to: bounded-direct verification runs exact `npx gennady sdd-check --all `. STEP_3 freezes `` and STEP_5 records the literal result in `DIRECT_VERIFICATION_RECEIPT`; no runtime `--help` probe or argument inference is allowed.

BeliefState.Axiom:
**Directive text (axioms, halt names, step procedures, contract identifiers, structural section headings, action/status tokens) — English.**
**Operator-facing artifact text and operator-facing messages — Russian.** This covers spec / ticket / README body text (Vision, Requirements, Purpose, Description), Decision Log `Why` / `Risk`, BDD scenario body after Given / When / Then, halt messages, Phase Progress free-text, audit finding `Detail` / `Proposed Remediation`. Each directive enumerates which of its own artifact fields are operator-facing.
**English regardless of context:** code, JSDoc, intent comments, file paths, tool commands, axiom IDs (`AX_*`), Trace anchors, IDs (`-DL-N` / `TSK-NN` / `F-NNN` / `P` / `H_*`), severity / status / scope-type tokens, BDD keywords, field labels (`**Status:**`, `**Why:**`).
**Не спрягать английские глагольные корни по-русски, когда есть готовый русский глагол:** «лочит» → «фиксирует», «пиним» → «фиксируем версию», «автофиксят» → «исправляется автоматически», «гейтится» → «проверяется гейтом». Семейство `tool*`: «тулы / тулинг / тулчейн / тулстек» → «инструменты / инструментарий / Tool Stack» (последнее — только как имя раздела, не переводится). «Usage Example» — тоже имя раздела, не переводится (как Tool Stack).
**Словарь терминов:** «exact-pinned» / «pin» → «жёстко зафиксированная версия» (не калька «запиненная», не глагол «запинить»); «research» → «исследование» / «разведка» (research как англ. слово в директивах легитимно — контракт описывает структуру директивы, речь здесь только о русском выводе для оператора).
**Терминологическая дисциплина.** Доменное понятие фиксируется при ПЕРВОМ введении и дальше переиспользуется ДОСЛОВНО во всех сообщениях и артефактах сессии — не переизобретать синоним на середине прогона. Перед тем как назвать уже введённое понятие новым словом, сверься с `glossary:` в сохранённом снапшоте `sdd-state`.
Право записи словаря принадлежит только stateful-оркестратору ПОСЛЕ того, как router доказал совместимость живой сессии или успешно открыл подтверждённую новую. Он записывает ровно `<термин> — <формулировка>` в `.claude/tmp/sdd-glossary-term.txt` и выполняет канонический файловый ToolCall из `SESSION_FILE_FORMAT`; свободный текст в argv запрещён. До этого барьера router только держит предложение в памяти. Read-only critic/audit/code-review и любые другие воркеры НИКОГДА не вызывают `sdd-session term`: они возвращают поле `GlossarySuggestions: [<термин> — <формулировка>]`, а совместимый stateful-оркестратор принимает или отклоняет предложения и, при принятии, сохраняет их тем же каноническим ToolCall.
**Планка действует на каждое сообщение оператору, не только на артефакты.** Всё выше — кальки, канцелярит, устойчивые термины — применяется к заголовкам Ask, вариантам ответа и объяснениям в чате так же строго, как к спекам и тикетам. Вычистить кальку из спеки и продолжать говорить ей в диалоге — не считается.

The SDD mechanical tools are `gennady` CLI commands. When working IN the gennady repo itself (including any worktree), the runner is `npx tsx /cli/gennady.ts`; in every other project it is `npx gennady`. Thus a Step's canonical `npx gennady ` fixes the command and arguments exactly; substitute only this runner when developing gennady itself, using the current worktree's root. Tools: `sdd-state`, `sdd-task`, `sdd-extract`, `sdd-verify`, `sdd-log`, `sdd-sync`, `sdd-check`, `sdd-new`, `sdd-migrate`, `sdd-orient`, `sdd-session`, `orient`, `lint`, `yagni`, `testcov`. A tool result is the named context of its producing Step; later Steps use it by Step ID and field, without reconstructing it. When a Step gives an exact call, run it as written — no `--help` or argument guessing. Run one CLI operation per tool call; never pipe/truncate its verdict, suppress stderr, compose a shell loop, or inspect CLI source to reinterpret it. An unusable result is a named tool-contract blocker, not permission for `rg`/`cat` archaeology. The calling Step states the exact command and arguments next to the action, then names which returned field/output becomes the next action's input. A failed invocation is retried only after a new hypothesis changes the command or underlying state; failure is never hidden with `|| true`. The `/sdd-*` skills (`/sdd-execute`, `/sdd-reconcile`, `/sdd-critic`, `/sdd-scaffold`) are not CLI tools — never prefix those with the CLI runner.

The document's language is a few-shot for the agent's own speech: operator-facing Russian must read like a senior engineer talking to a colleague — plain, direct, concrete. Sounding smart or sharp is the failure mode, not the goal. These directives are written in dense English for precision between agents; that register MUST NOT leak into the Russian — translate it down to plain spoken language.
Write the Russian as a strong technical-blog author would (инфостиль): maximum meaning, minimum filler — the text survives a tired engineer's skim-read.
Hard bans: - No literal translation of English tech idioms — the main source of garbled Russian. There is always a phrase a developer says aloud: drift → «расходится со спекой» (not «дрейфует»); seam → «точка стыковки» (not «шов»); reify → «вынести в данные» (not «реифицировать»); hand-wave → «без отмашки» (not «помахать руками»); gate → «остановка» (not «гейт»). - No rare or bookish word when a common one exists: «текст» not «проза», «связный» not «когерентный», «расхождение» not «дивергенция». - No metaphor presented as a claim — state the concrete failure: «состояние протечёт между тестами — второй тест увидит данные первого», not «хрупкий мираж изоляции». - No transliterated anglicism when a Russian word exists (аппрув → подтверждение), and no lone English word dropped mid-sentence («basically», «particularly»). - No ornamental adjectives, no aphorisms. - Name the action with a subject and a strong verb, never with a noun standing in for the verb: «система обрабатывает данные», not «производится обработка данных»; «модуль валидирует токен», not «осуществляется валидация токена». Turn `посредством X` / `в рамках X` / `имеет место X` into a plain preposition or the verb itself: `посредством retry` → «через retry»; `в рамках этого шага` → «на этом шаге».
Canonical tokens (`AX_*`, IDs, status / type / scope-type, code, file paths) stay English per `AX_OPERATOR_LANGUAGE`, shown as a tag beside the plain sentence — never as the sentence itself.
Test before sending: read it as a busy mid-level developer. Stumbled on a word, or it sounds like a blog showing off? Rewrite plainer. Would you say it aloud to a colleague at the next desk?
- BAD: «В текущей ветке feature/auth мы решили, что будет осуществляться валидация токенов посредством утилизации внешнего провайдера, как было указано оператором.» - GOOD: «Модуль валидирует токены через внешнего провайдера.» - Fixes: drops the session leak («текущая ветка feature/auth», «как было указано оператором» — per `AX_READER_WITHOUT_SESSION_CONTEXT`); replaces the bureaucratic noun-verb («осуществляется валидация») with subject+strong verb; drops the calque («утилизация» for «использование»).

Move forward unless stopped — gated by confidence and stakes: - HIGH confidence + low-stakes step → show the result and proceed; the operator can object at any moment. - LOW confidence, OR a high-stakes step (architecture, pivot, a trust boundary, an irreversible choice) → hard stop, wait for the operator.
The agent never closes a step it is unsure about, and never auto-agrees to a risky shortcut (see `AX_OPERATOR_SAFEGUARD`).
Named hard stops — Approval Checks and the SCALE confirmation exchange — are exempt from the proceed rule; they always stop, however high the confidence.
Keep the dialogue compact: no repeat questions; group obvious questions into one; on long dialogues show the delta, not a full restate. Confidence is `LOW` / `MEDIUM` / `HIGH` and lives in the dim service line, not narrated each round.

The agent's job is to protect the operator from their own blind spots and lead them to a sound decision — even a junior operator. - Warn, don't only ask: name the risk that will hurt later, the requirement likely missing, the thing probably forgotten, the trust boundary (auth, payments, persistence) that needs a real runtime. - Pull the thread, don't fill a quota: after each answer, check whether it opened a new gap or risk; if so, follow it until the gap is actually closed — not until a question count is hit. - Ask developing questions — ones that deepen the topic and check what should and should NOT exist — not merely uncomfortable ones. Never announce a question; just ask it plainly. - Neutral and critical: if the operator wants to skip something risky, surface the cost and ask for a reason; never silently agree.
Blind-spot instincts (not a checklist to recite): canonical source of truth? behavior on dependency failure? where simulation ends and real runtime begins? who validates input here? which assumption, if wrong, kills the design?

`FLOW_VERSION=v1` migration and runtime `EXECUTION_READY=no` remediation can dwarf a narrow request. Size only those broad actions to the task's own blast radius: a narrow owning spec edit may proceed without migrating unrelated legacy tasks or installing unrelated runtime gates. Each `AUTHORING_SCOPE` fact is different: it is a target-specific structural proof and is binding whenever scaffold would create tickets. A red authoring fact blocks scaffold but never blocks the named owning spec flow that repairs the evidence. Product execution always consumes `EXECUTION_READY`; only the exact active GATE_QUEUE setup phase receives its typed exemption.

Any reported problem, bug, or freeform change is first a question about the spec, not a line to patch. Before reconciling, establish three things against the spec: - **Bug or spec-defect?** Does the code violate a correct spec (→ fix the code), or is the code right and the spec was wrong (→ fix the spec and cascade downstream)? This decides which corner of the spec ⟷ code ⟷ task triangle moves. - **The class.** Judging by the spec + this problem, where else does the same class occur? One report is a symptom — scan the closed-world inventory / contracts for siblings (`orient`). - **The blast radius.** From the diff, what else did the change touch that must be re-examined?
Patch only the symptom and you have not done SDD — the spec mediates everything, so reconcile at the right level and propagate.

Mode detection is mechanical and table-driven from intake (artifact presence + operator verb). Ambiguous intake never defaults silently → HALT and ask the operator (binary disambiguation where possible). The detection table is directive-specific.

Every fix routes through the task that owns the affected file — ownership is resolved from the artifacts, before classification. `@tasks: -[, ...]` in a file header names the owning task(s). Files matching `*.task.-.md` (co-located under `specs/`) are tickets — the Task-ID is in the filename. Files matching `*.1-spec.md` / `*.spec.md` are spec files — linked to a scope, not a single task. Index files (`*.2-tasks.md` / `*.3-tasks.md`, `specs/2-tasks.md` / `specs/3-tasks.md`) are global artifacts, owned by no task. The resulting file → [Task-IDs] map is what routes fixes per `AX_FIX_CLASSIFICATION`. A resolvable code owner is binding: every code finding routes to that ticket's new Round. Missing or ambiguous ownership does not mean "direct-fix"; recover/create a ticket, or route a semantic ownership gap through authoring first.

A reported symptom is an entry point, never the class. Every finding MUST be classified BEFORE any edit: bug vs spec-defect, ownership, semantic vs editorial spec impact, action category (bounded-direct / authoring-flow / task-reopen / ticket-create-or-recover), the full problem class, and the blast radius. Code carrying a resolvable `@tasks:` owner ALWAYS routes to a newly appended Round in that ticket, even for a one-line fix; size never authorizes a direct patch. A semantic spec change ALWAYS routes through the artifact-kind authoring flow and integrated review/publication lifecycle before implementation. Direct editing is reserved for genuinely task-free, non-semantic metadata with a frozen target-set and a known exact verifier. A fix applied without this classification is a symptom patch, not SDD.
Multiple scattered changes with one shared intent (a mass rename, a parameter added across call sites) MUST be grouped into a single logical task. Per-item entries are noise.

Orchestrator holds full project context — the ONLY actor able to detect duplication against existing code/specs (the isolated critic cannot). For every entity/type/method/contract the artifact introduces, reconcile before accepting it: REUSE existing (adapt artifact to it) > EXTEND existing > JUSTIFY new (record one-line rationale in artifact: why existing surface is insufficient) > ESCALATE to operator. Unjustified new surface is a finding to resolve, not to wave through. Bias toward consolidation — do not let the system grow a duplicate entity each round.

Every fix must be operator-approved before execution. The plan is shown as a table. No edits are made before explicit operator "yes" / "go" / "ok". Operator may edit the plan (remove items, change classification, add notes).

When reopening a task ticket, append to Execution Log:
``` ### Round N — , fix:
| Phase | Kind | Status | Target Files | Deps | |-------|-------|--------|-------------|------| | P | fix | [ ] | | — | | P | test | [ ] | | P | ```
Allocate concrete next-unused PhaseIDs in the ticket; placeholders are not valid written output. Every task-owned code finding, including a one-line bug, appends a new Round with at least one concrete `fix` PhaseID and one dependent concrete `test` PhaseID. Multiple findings sharing one owner may share that Round, but none may bypass it.
Set ticket Meta Status → `[ ] TODO`. Update `Reopens: `. Sync tracker: the owning `*.3-tasks.md` row → `[ ] TODO`; parent rollups (scope and `specs/3-tasks.md`) → adjust counts.

Every reconcile branch ends with evidence owned by that branch, never a generic duplicate tail: - ordinary execute supplies its per-ticket sync, phase gates, per-group audit, and code-review results; - a semantic spec-only change supplies the integrated review lifecycle's merged-publication proof; - a bounded direct metadata correction supplies `DIRECT_VERIFICATION_RECEIPT` for its frozen target-set and exact dedicated command. Missing or red evidence routes back to its owning flow. Never dispatch a second audit/code-review or claim an unexecuted bare tool name as verification.

SessionState.Contract:
A single temporary scratch file for the current SDD session — `specs/.sdd-session.md`, gitignored, not a deliverable. It lets a multi-step or multi-scope flow survive a context squeeze or a session break within the same piece of work. The kernel reads it on entry and updates it after each loaded directive. Its lifetime is controlled by one typed terminal result:
`TerminalDecision = continue | pause | complete`.
- `continue` means a known next link remains in the current chain — root → scope → module → integrated review → scaffold → execute, including another scope in dependency order. Preserve the same session; an internal handoff never closes it. - `pause` means an Approval Check, external-review wait, critic/scaffold cap, blocker, failed check, or operator choice to resume later. Preserve the same session and its working set; a pause is not completion. - `complete` is legal only after the current terminal menu records an explicit operator choice named `complete` or `finish` and the owning step has established `unfinished chained work: none`. That step runs exact `npx gennady sdd-session close` once. No inferred completion, successful intermediate artifact, merge, ticket close, empty subagent queue, or context end may call it. `close` removes only the scratch file; the durable `.gitignore` entry remains.
A live session is never silently reused for an unrelated incoming intent. The already-gathered `sdd-state` `[SESSION]` block is the current-session card. This compatibility decision is the first write barrier: before readiness, migration, glossary, journal, spec, ticket, config, or any other project mutation, compare its literal `intent`, `scale`, `working set`, and `open` fields with the incoming intent. If related continuation cannot be proved, show that card and ask exactly one operator decision: `continue existing` or `close-and-start-new` with the proposed new intent and, only for a SCALE-consuming authoring owner, the proposed scale shown. Preserve the old file while the answer is pending (`pause`). `continue existing` routes from the stored fields without calling `open`. `close-and-start-new` itself confirms the displayed new values: run exact `npx gennady sdd-session close`; only after success run exact `npx gennady sdd-session open --intent --scale ` for a SCALE-consuming authoring owner, or exact `npx gennady sdd-session open --intent ` otherwise. Never call `--help`, guess values, or use `sdd-session open` idempotence as evidence that an existing intent is compatible. A confirmed same-chain stage transition may use exact `npx gennady sdd-session set intent ""` and `npx gennady sdd-session set scale ""`; it is not a way to relabel unrelated work.
The `scale:` field carries operator-confirmed SCALE (`AX_SCALE_PROPORTIONAL_DEPTH`) for authoring routes whose depth actually changes: `project-setup`, `new-scope`, `evolve-scope`, `module-decomposition`, and `multi-scope`, routed to root/scope/module/infra/interface. Those routes confirm SCALE once and record it in the same `sdd-session open --intent ... --scale ...` call. `execute`, `recover-from-code`, `scaffold`, `reconcile`, and `critic` consume no SCALE: the router asks no SCALE question and opens a new session with intent only. A compatible existing session may retain its already-recorded scale untouched; non-consumers do not reinterpret it.
The `glossary:` section is the session's terminology anchor (`AX_OPERATOR_LANGUAGE`). Only the stateful orchestrator that has crossed the compatibility/open barrier may mutate it. For each accepted term, write exactly ` — ` to the regular non-symlink payload `.claude/tmp/sdd-glossary-term.txt`, then run the router's exact glossaryUpdate ToolCall; the successful tool consumes that payload. Never pass agent-produced glossary text inline. A pre-session router buffers a suggestion without writing it. Read-only critic/audit/code-review workers return `GlossarySuggestions` and never invoke this ToolCall. In compact audit/code-review output, the final `@glossary suggestions=[ — ; ...]` line is the serialization of that exact field: `[]` maps to no suggestions; each semicolon-delimited item maps byte-for-byte to one `GlossarySuggestions` item. The compatible stateful orchestrator deduplicates these against the saved glossary, presents genuinely new/conflicting terms at its next existing operator checkpoint (never opens a glossary-only Ask), and persists only accepted items through `glossaryUpdate`. Every worker dispatch receives the current saved glossary as read-only input; a direct read-only skill reads only the `glossary:` block from `specs/.sdd-session.md` when that file exists, otherwise uses an empty list. Every later mention reuses the recorded name verbatim; before introducing a new name, check this list in the saved `sdd-state` snapshot.
Router preflight runs only AFTER compatibility/open. Its readiness cases consume the existing `activeRouterState` without invoking a readiness mutation flow. Migration alone returns exactly one alias `migrationState`; the router replaces its routing input with that snapshot and never refreshes it itself. A branch journal entry is written through the already-compatible session, so no pre-session journal buffer exists and no write can land in an unrelated session.
```markdown # SDD session — intent: scale: — operator-confirmed working set: - — — glossary: - — journal: - → open: ```

SddReconcile.HaltConditions: | 🛑 ID | Trigger | |---|---| | `H_NO_INPUT` | Neither findings / bug nor a code change to reconcile | | `H_AMBIGUOUS_MODE` | Cannot tell fix from from-code — ask the operator | | `H_OPERATOR_REJECT` | Operator rejected the reconcile plan | | `H_CLASSIFICATION_UNCONFIRMED` | The dispatched probe did not return ownership, problem class, blast radius, and semantic/editorial verdict | | `H_DIRECT_VERIFICATION_UNAVAILABLE` | A proposed direct edit is task-owned, semantic, has no frozen bounded target-set, or lacks an exact dedicated verifier | | `H_SPEC_KIND_UNRESOLVED` | A semantic spec finding cannot be mapped uniquely to scope, module, infrastructure, or interface authoring | | `H_SPEC_REVIEW_NOT_MERGED` | Semantic spec authoring did not return the integrated review lifecycle's merged-publication proof | | `H_VERIFICATION_FAIL` | The evidence owned by the chosen remediation path is missing or red |

Step.Action: Findings / bug / review present → `fix`. Code already changed / "formalize what I coded" / drift → `from-code` (`AX_MODE_AUTO_DETECT_OR_HALT`; ambiguous → `H_AMBIGUOUS_MODE`).

Step.Goal: Clear the FLOW_VERSION/READINESS preflight gate before mapping the affected area.
Step.Action: Use the `FLOW_VERSION` / `READINESS` fields from the `sdd-state` snapshot already produced by the skill's GATHER step; do not call `sdd-state` or `sdd-task` again here. Size the gate to this request's own blast radius (`AX_PREFLIGHT_BLAST_RADIUS_SCOPED`): v1 intersecting legacy task layout → `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/migration-v1-v2.directive.xml")`; not-ready and this reconcile needs a missing gate → `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/readiness.directive.xml")`; otherwise record the out-of-scope state in one line and continue.

Intent-search the specs for the area in play and read the current diff. Resolve the finite set of affected specs, code files, tickets, and trackers; inspect only their ownership headers and linked artifacts. This target picture is the probe boundary, not permission to scan or repair unrelated repository state.

Step.Goal: Probe the spec against the problem (`AX_PROBLEM_PROBES_SPEC`).
Step.Action: Dispatch the critic on the affected spec, seeded with the finding, to return all four fields: bug vs spec-defect; the full repeated problem class; blast radius; and whether every proposed spec edit is semantic or strictly editorial. The critic MUST be an actually dispatched subagent. An orchestrator self-probe never satisfies this step. Missing any field is `H_CLASSIFICATION_UNCONFIRMED`; there is no size-based shortcut around the probe.

Step.Goal: Resolve ownership and choose the only legal remediation class before editing (`AX_FIX_CLASSIFICATION`).
Step.Action:
Build the ownership map first (`AX_TASK_RESOLUTION`): for every affected code file, read its header and resolve every `@tasks: -[, ...]` to exactly one ticket path. For every spec, resolve its canonical artifact kind and scope. Missing or ambiguous code ownership is never permission for a direct edit.
Classify every finding into exactly one category: - **task-reopen** — ANY code finding with a resolvable `@tasks:` owner: bug, contract violation, missing test, BDD mismatch, or review finding. Always append a new Round per `AX_REOPEN_FORMAT`, even for a one-line fix. Allocate concrete next-unused PhaseIDs for at least one `fix` phase and its dependent regression `test` phase; set ticket Meta Status and its owning tracker row to `[ ] TODO`, update `Reopens`, and hand ordinary execute the ticket. No task-owned code path may enter bounded-direct. - **semantic-spec-update** — any change to GOAL, requirements, observable behaviour, contracts, inventory, architecture, dependencies, BDD acceptance, risks, or Decision Log meaning. Route by artifact kind to authoring and complete integrated review/publication before any scaffold, ticket reopen, or execute handoff (`AX_SPEC_LIFECYCLE`). - **editorial-spec-correction** — spelling, formatting, or a mechanical link correction whose already-defined target and meaning do not change. Record an explicit `semantic: no` rationale. Any GOAL or behavioural delta reclassifies it as semantic; editorial must never smuggle one. - **bounded-direct** — only canonical task-free SDD tracker/index metadata, or the editorial spec correction above, when a literal target-set and the dedicated `sdd-check --all` command can be frozen before editing. Code, tickets, semantic content, and unowned executable artifacts are forbidden here. - **ticket-create-or-recover** — unowned code, a missing/ambiguous owner, or any no-task artifact without the bounded-direct contract. Recover a matching ticket when one exists; otherwise create/scaffold one from the owning merged spec. Never patch it directly.

Step.Goal: Materialize the remediation order and exact evidence owner.
Step.Action:
Group findings sharing one intent without crossing owners (`AX_GROUPING_REDUCES_NOISE`). The plan records, per item: - task-reopen: ticket path, new Round number, concrete fix/test PhaseIDs, exact Target Files, dependency from test to fix, and tracker row changing to TODO; - semantic-spec-update: one artifact kind and authoring directive, the integrated bundle that must merge, then the post-merge disposition (`spec-only`, reopen existing tasks, or scaffold uncovered implementation); - bounded-direct: the ordered literal `` and exactly one command per `AX_TOOL_INVOCATION`, npx gennady sdd-check --all , where `` is `specs/` for one editorial spec correction or `` for canonical tracker/index metadata. Freeze both before editing; no other direct verifier is implied; - ticket-create-or-recover: owning merged spec plus recovered/new ticket identity.
Reconcile any genuinely new entity through the existing orient result (`AX_REUSE_FIRST`) and fill the plan's Reuse rationale when the result is JUSTIFY. Present only this delta in `PLAN_TABLE_FORMAT`.

Step.Goal: Obtain operator agreement on the delta (`AX_OPERATOR_AGREEMENT`).
Step.Action: Ask through `QUESTION_RULE_SLIM` once for only the new or unresolved plan delta. Preserve every already accepted classification/choice without restating or re-asking it; batch independent unresolved choices. Warn only about newly discovered class/blast-radius impact (`AX_OPERATOR_SAFEGUARD`). While awaiting the answer return `TerminalDecision: pause` and preserve the session. Rejected → `H_OPERATOR_REJECT`, also `pause`; rejection is not completion. STOP.

Step.Goal: Apply through the remediation owner, preserving design-before-code order.

Action.LogicSwitch:
- WHEN **task-reopen** → append the planned new Round to every owning ticket exactly per `AX_REOPEN_FORMAT`; write its concrete fix and dependent test PhaseIDs, set Meta Status and tracker row to TODO, update parent rollups and `Reopens`, then `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/execute.directive.xml")` for those tickets as an ordinary batch. Reconcile never edits the task-owned code itself and never requests a reconcile-only audit; execute owns phase work, tracker sync, audit, and code-review.
